## What happened (2026-11-09)

CI run 42590449630 (Dependabot pm-toolchain PR #203, head 1996b06) had `test (22)` and `test (26)` sitting in **Full Bun release gate** from 09:36Z and 09:54Z until the orchestrator cancelled them at 11:55Z. That is more than two hours with no output. The last test line before the hang was `✔ diagnostic output is bounded and never echoes source text or machine paths (8262 ms)`, so something after it never exits under Bun: a child process, an open handle, or a test that waits forever.

The CI jobs set no `timeout-minutes`, so GitHub's 6-hour default applies. On a shared free-tier account, two hung jobs starve every other repository's CI. 77 runs were queued fleet-wide while this happened.

## Fix

1. Find the test or teardown that keeps the Bun gate alive after the last test. For example, run `bun run release:check` locally with a timer, or with `--test-timeout` and active-handle reporting. Fix the leak, and add a regression that fails when a handle stays open.
2. Add `timeout-minutes` to every CI job (`test`, `release gate`), sized at about twice the slowest healthy run, so a hang fails fast instead of holding runners.
3. This repository is the starter for new packages, so carry the timeout into the template.

## Acceptance

- The Bun release gate exits within its normal duration on both Node lines.
- Every job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has `timeout-minutes`.
Bun release gate hangs after its last test and CI jobs have no timeout (two runners held for 2+ hours)

value.text: Round G sharding plan, from the cancelled-run measurements: the quick suite never completes one hosted job (test 22: 389 tests in 1799 s then cancelled; test 26: 431 tests in 1797 s then cancelled, both inside the coverage run; static gates take ~10 s). Per-test totals from the logs: the quick Node 22 suite is ~2100-2400 s serial and is dominated by test/sdk-contracts.test.ts (~1381 s alone), which no file-based shard can fit under 12 min. Restructure: (1) split sdk-contracts.test.ts into a shared support module plus five part files sized from measured test durations (parts ~235-350 s each, published-bounds tests grouped to avoid repeated registry installs); (2) Node 22: non-required quick-shard matrix (5 shards, node --test --test-shard=k/5 --test-concurrency=1, PM_TEST_DEPTH=quick, same build/setup), required test (22) becomes an always()-aggregate that requires every shard success on code PRs and the docs gates otherwise; (3) Node 26: non-coverage release-gate steps in one job (they measure ~10 s), coverage run sharded 5 ways via a new --shard mode of scripts/coverage-gate.ts that writes per-shard JSON reports, plus a --merge gate that merges per-file line, branch and function hit counts (sum; covered iff any shard hit) and enforces the unchanged 100 percent thresholds plus the source-presence check on the union; fixture test proves sharded-then-merged equals unsharded on a real fixture project; required test (26) aggregates static, shards and merge. npm run coverage and npm run release:check stay intact for local/deep use. Round-robin shard assignment simulated on measured per-file times: worst shard ~460 s tests + setup, under the 12-minute projection. Risks: the eight tail files never completed any logged run (estimated 200-400 s total), so per-shard projections there are estimates; first CI run of this head will measure them.
